title: First Sunday of Lent
hookLine: the gospel is always the temptation in the desert
tomorrow: The Chair of Saint Peter (22 February)

cards: The Sunday readings change on a three-year cycle: Matthew one year, Mark the next, Luke the third. Most of the gospels change from one year to the next.
But on the first Sunday of Lent, whichever year it is, the story is the same: Jesus, alone in the wilderness, hungry, and tempted. The Church has fixed it there like a signpost at the trailhead.
Before you walk the forty days, here's who walked them first, and how it went.

teach.b: Right after his baptism, the voice from heaven still ringing, the Spirit leads Jesus into the desert.
He fasts forty days and forty nights, and afterward, the text says simply, he was hungry. Forty isn't a random number. Israel wandered forty years in the wilderness.
Moses stayed forty days on the mountain. Elijah walked forty days to the mountain of God. Jesus steps into the same desert his people knew.
Then the tempter comes, three times.
First, the hungry man: if thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread.
He answers from Deuteronomy, in the Douay-Rheims: "Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God."
Second, on the pinnacle of the temple: throw yourself down, the angels will catch you. Third, on a high mountain, all the kingdoms of the world, his for one act of worship.
Each time he answers from Deuteronomy, the book of Israel's own desert years.
Three temptations, people have noticed, that touch almost everyone: comfort, attention and power.
Mark tells it in two verses and adds a detail no other Gospel has: he was with the wild beasts, and the angels ministered to him.

teach.h: NOT IN BREAD ALONE DOTH MAN LIVE.
teach.b: On this Sunday, in many dioceses, adults preparing for baptism at Easter are presented to the bishop and enrolled, the Rite of Election. Their forty days begin with his. Lent, in Latin, is Quadragesima, the fortieth.
The whole season is shaped like this desert.

how: On the First Sunday of Lent the gospel is always the temptation of Jesus in the desert, and in many dioceses the bishop celebrates the Rite of Election for adults preparing for baptism at Easter.

o: Latin for the forty hours of prayer before Easter
Latin for the fast before Christmas in Advent
Latin for the fortieth: the Church's name for Lent

p: all the kingdoms of the world

s: the first Sunday of Lent has a different story each year
every year it's the temptation, from Matthew, Mark or Luke.
Mark says Jesus was with the wild beasts
and the angels ministered to him.
Jesus answers the tempter with his own new sayings
each time he answers with a line from Deuteronomy.

games.q: you've fasted forty days and you're starving. a voice says: if you're the Son of God, turn these stones into bread. what do you say?
o: make the bread; there's no harm in eating.
not in bread alone doth man live.
games.why: he answers from Deuteronomy 8:3: not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word from the mouth of God.

practice: Let it get quiet and ask what your wilderness is right now, a loneliness, a waiting, a craving, a fear, and name it plainly, in one word if you can.

Then ask which of the three pulls hardest there, comfort, attention or power, without judging, just naming. If you pray, ask for the angels Mark mentions to minister to you; if not, stay with what you named.

wordCard.voice: Quadragesima, the fortieth. The Church's Latin name for Lent, the forty days that begin each year with Jesus tempted in the desert. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the fortieth (day), the Church's Latin name for Lent.

carryVoice: Your line: forty days. He walked them first, and the season follows him. That's day six hundred fifty-two.
